summary: An automated AI curation agent in a biomedical knowledge-base repository began a beginner-friendly task before the new human contributor it was meant for could do it. A maintainer apologized and opened a policy issue about agents taking newcomer tasks too quickly.
technical_summary: An AI agent integrated into a GitHub workflow picked up and worked on an issue intended as a learning task for a new contributor. The gap was missing guardrails on which tasks agents may claim. The excerpt is only an issue page, so details come from the AIID description.
notes: The only report is a GitHub issue page, not coverage; tags rely on the AIID description.

summary: Kenya's Social Health Authority used a machine-learning means test to set health insurance premiums. Investigators found it was designed to overcharge the poorest households, and reported that some critically ill people could not get treatment because they could not pay.
technical_summary: A model predicts household income from 43 survey-style variables such as roof material and toilet type, and a share of the predicted income becomes the annual premium. Reporters reconstructed the model from released data and found it systematically overestimated income for poor households. Training data and indicators were not initially disclosed.

summary: An investigation of Germany's Schufa credit scores found they favored older and female consumers and people who changed address less often. Some people received lower scores under newer versions of the algorithm, and the scoring method is a trade secret.
technical_summary: A proprietary credit-scoring algorithm turns consumer data into a risk score used for banking, rentals and contracts. Crowdsourced credit reports revealed demographic skews and inconsistent results across four algorithm versions, with little transparency about how scores are produced.
